records.Entity / project type: hardware signer family / companion wallet ecosystem
records.Concise description: SatoshiLabs' pioneering hardware-wallet family, combining open-source firmware/design with on-device signing and current Secure Element-equipped models.
records.Deeper researched summary: Trezor created the first mass-market hardware wallet lineage and remains an active signer family managed through Trezor Suite and compatible third-party wallets. Current Safe-series devices use Secure Elements while preserving an open-source design philosophy; some models have Bitcoin-only firmware editions. The family spans multiple models rather than requiring one MSC profile per device.
Creators / founders: Alena Vranova — early SatoshiLabs co-founder / CEO
records.Launch / history: Prototype work began in 2012–2013 and the Trezor Model One shipped to customers in 2014. The current Safe 3, Safe 5 and Safe 7 generation remained active in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Trezor established the commercial hardware-wallet category and remains a foundational reference for open-source hardware signing and recovery standards.
Important technical or cultural characte: Bitcoin-only firmware editions on supported models
Coin control and Tor in Trezor Suite
records.Verification basis: Current Trezor product pages and SatoshiLabs history verify active Bitcoin support, current hardware architecture and product-family lineage.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not say Trezor hardware stores bitcoin; it secures private keys.
Secure Element presence varies across Trezor generations; do not retroactively describe every historical Trezor model as having one.
All current models are consolidated into one Trezor profile.

records.Concise description: Coinkite's Bitcoin-only hardware signer family built around air-gapped PSBT workflows, dual Secure Elements and deep advanced-wallet interoperability.
records.Deeper researched summary: COLDCARD is a Bitcoin-only signer designed for users who may never connect the device directly to a host computer. Current Mk5 and Q models can sign PSBTs via microSD, NFC, QR on supported hardware, USB or virtual-disk workflows, and use dual Secure Elements to protect seed material. It can participate in multisig and works with independent wallet coordinators rather than requiring a proprietary companion app.
Creators / founders: Rodolfo Novak (NVK) — Coinkite co-founder / public project lead
records.Launch / history: Announced for preorder in 2017 with first-generation units shipping in 2018; COLDCARD evolved through Mk-series devices and the Q, with Mk5/Q current in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: It is a central Bitcoin-only hardware signer for advanced cold-storage, air-gapped and multisig workflows and helped normalize PSBT-based hardware interoperability.
records.Verification basis: Current COLDCARD product documentation and firmware history verify active models, signing transports, Secure Element design and Bitcoin-only scope.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not say COLDCARD stores bitcoin; it protects/signs with private keys.
Air-gapped operation is a workflow choice and does not by itself constitute a universal security rating.

records.Concise description: Foundation's fully open-source Bitcoin-only hardware signer family, with Passport Core using QR/microSD communication and no data-capable USB or wireless link.
records.Deeper researched summary: Foundation Passport is a Bitcoin-only signer designed around inspectable hardware/software and air-gapped transaction exchange. The current Passport Core communicates through its camera/QR codes and microSD, while its USB-C port is power-only; a Secure Element protects key material. Foundation also develops Envoy as a companion wallet, but Passport works with third-party PSBT coordinators.
records.Launch / history: Foundation announced the original Passport in 2020. The second-generation product evolved into the current Passport Core branding; Foundation continued active firmware and product development in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: It is an important open-hardware Bitcoin signer combining consumer-grade UX with a deliberately air-gapped transaction model and broad coordinator interoperability.
Important technical or cultural characte: Envoy companion app plus third-party wallet support
records.Verification basis: Current Foundation product/docs and open-source firmware/hardware repositories verify active status, current Passport Core name and signing architecture.
Research notes / uncertainties: The canonical entity remains Foundation Passport; Passport Core is the current family/model name rather than a separate MSC entity.
Do not claim Miniscript support from stale roadmap text unless reverified at publication time.
Do not say Passport stores bitcoin; it secures/signs with private keys.

records.Entity / project type: hardware signer family / companion wallet ecosystem
records.Concise description: Shift Crypto's Swiss hardware-signer family, including Bitcoin-only editions and the current BitBox02 Nova with open-source firmware and a dual-chip Secure Element design.
records.Deeper researched summary: The BitBox lineage began with Digital Bitbox/BitBox01 and now centers on BitBox02 and BitBox02 Nova. The Bitcoin-only firmware edition reduces supported code to Bitcoin, while multi-asset editions remain available. Nova adds iOS/iPadOS support, Bluetooth and an EAL6+ certified secure chip while retaining microSD backup and open-source firmware.
Creators / founders: Douglas Bakkum — co-founder / BitBox lineage creator
Jonas Schnelli — co-founder / BitBox lineage creator
records.Launch / history: The BitBox project began in 2015; BitBox01 reached market in 2016, followed by BitBox02 and the BitBox02 Nova generation introduced in 2025.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: BitBox is an important hardware-signer family for its open-source firmware, Bitcoin-only edition, microSD backup model and interoperability with Bitcoin multisig software.
Important technical or cultural characte: BitBox02 Nova supports desktop, Android and iOS/iPadOS
Optional Bluetooth on Nova can be disabled
records.Verification basis: Current BitBox product pages and company history verify family consolidation, open-source firmware, Bitcoin-only edition and Nova platform/security details.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not describe the hardware device as storing bitcoin; it secures signing keys.
The BitBox01 is historical family lineage and should not receive a separate canonical profile.
